_readme: This file maps Ariba JSON onto NFA fields. It is the ONE place to change
when your realm's field names turn out to be different - no Python edits.
Each field lists candidate paths, tried IN ORDER; the first one that yields
a non-empty value wins. So you can APPEND a newly discovered path rather
than replacing a guess, and both realms keep working.
The paths below are STARTING GUESSES. To find the real ones, run a dump
(the 'Dump raw JSON' button, or: dev.bat --dump YOUR_EVENT_ID), open the
generated *_paths.csv in Excel, and match on the sample values.

user_department._note: Mapped to the event's Department. Ariba returns it as a list shaped like commodities ({uniqueName, domain, name}); the singular forms below cover realms that return a single object instead. Multiple departments join with ', '.

equipment_area._note: Mapped to the event's commodity. Multiple commodities join with ', '. Swap to commodities[*].uniqueName for the UNSPSC code instead of the name, or put regions[*].name first to use the site/location.

plant._note: Ariba carries Plant as a term on each LINE ITEM (fieldId 'Plant', a MasterDataType whose value is {simpleValue}), not on the event header. The header row therefore reads it from the items; identical values across lines are collapsed to one, and genuinely different plants are listed together.

doc_date._note: The date printed under the letterhead. Falls back to today.

_note: The awarded total, from GET /events/{id}/awards. Fills 'Total Cost of
this NFA' and takes precedence over the figure derived from the ranked
L1 vendor, because it is what Ariba actually awarded.
The Totals roll-up row is reached as item > terms > Total > moneyValue >
amount. Ariba names terms by both fieldId and title and wraps values
inconsistently, so several spellings are tried in order.
VERIFY THESE PATHS: the realm this was written against had no awarded
event (awards returned an empty payload), so they are inferred from the
term shapes seen elsewhere in the same API. Dump an awarded event and
correct them from the paths CSV if needed.
If more than one value resolves they are summed, and the document says so.
_scenario_note: Used only when nothing has actually been awarded. Award scenarios are
MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE alternatives - Best Bid, Best Savings and so on - so
these are never summed; one is picked and the document states that the
figure is a projection rather than an award.
awarded_value._scenario_all_note: Every scenario total, so the alternatives can be named rather than quietly discarded.

_note: Priced lines of the event, used by the item-wise supplier price section.
GET /events/{id}/items returns every row including sections and headers;
only rows carrying a PRICE term are treated as priced line items.

title: title
description
name
fields._last_po_price_note: GITASHORTSTRINGIFZ000311 is this realm's internal id for the 'Last PO Price' field. Another realm will use a different id - match it by its title or by sample value in the paths CSV.
fields._total_price_note: Asked for as 'Total Value'; the field this realm actually exposes is TOTALCOST, titled 'Total Cost'. Both spellings are tried.

_note: Per-supplier, per-line pricing from GET /events/{id}/supplierBids.
Confirmed against Doc89045043: one entry per bidder per item, each
carrying item.terms with PRICE, QUANTITY and EXTENDEDPRICE.
A bid names its bidder only by 'invitationId' (an email-like id), never
by company name, so 'vendor' below resolves to that id and is then joined
back to event.supplierInvitations to get the organisation name.
Each bidder also has a 'Totals' roll-up entry. It is ignored because its
itemId matches no line item - counting it would double every total.
root_paths is tried in order until one yields a list. Each element is one
vendor. If your realm returns one row PER LINE ITEM per vendor, that is
fine - rows are grouped by vendor name and their amounts summed.

name: organization.name
supplierName
supplier.name
mainContact.orgName
vendorName
name
fields._invitation_id_note: How supplierBids refers to this vendor; the join key between a bid and a company name.
